stem.text: A particle moves along the x-axis. Its velocity at time t seconds is \( v(t) = - 2 t^{3} + 3 t^{2} - 2 t + 1 \) meters per second, for \( t \ge 0 \). Find the speed of the particle at time t = 2, and determine whether the speed is increasing or decreasing at that time. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The speed is 7 meters per second, and it is increasing at that time, because \( v(2) = -7 \) and \( a(2) = -14 \) have the same sign.

worked_solution.text: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, \( a(t) = - 6 t^{2} + 6 t - 2 \), so \( a(2) = -14 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: acceleration is the derivative of velocity

worked_solution.text: The speed is \( \left|v(2)\right| = 7 \) meters per second.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed is the absolute value of velocity

worked_solution.text: Because \( v(2) = -7 \) and \( a(2) = -14 \) have the same sign, the speed of the particle is increasing at t = 2.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed increases when velocity and acceleration share a sign
